chunks: My father, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Ahmad ibn Idris narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ahmad ibn Hilal, from Ibn Sinan, from Hurayz, from Fudayl ibn Yasar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

That which is necessitated is not declared Mahram through breastfeeding. He said: I said: And what is the necessitated? He said: The mother of the raiser, or a hired wet nurse, or a purchased servant. And whatever is like that is established upon it.

key_terms.مَجْبُورٌ: Necessitated / Compulsory (in this context, referring to non-biological but legally recognized nursing)

ai.seo_question: Does breastfeeding by a hired wet nurse or purchased servant create mahram kinship in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq records Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifying that breastfeeding establishes legal kinship (mahramiyah) only when it is 'necessitated' (majburan), specifically citing hired wet nurses, purchased servants, or the mother of the raiser as valid sources. This ruling distinguishes these formalized relationships from casual or informal nursing, ensuring the legal implications for marriage prohibitions are strictly defined within Shia fiqh. The emphasis on 'necessity' reflects the practical realities of pre-modern household structures where wet nursing was a common economic and social arrangement.

en.basel-kadem: 1.	My father, may Allah grant him mercy, said: We were told by Ahmad bin Idrees, from Muhammed bin Ahmad, from Ahmad bin Hilal, from Ibn Sinan, from Huraiz, from Fudail bin Yasar, from Abu Abdillah, peace be upon him, that he said:

It is not to declare as Mahram [1] from breastfeeding except for that which is necessitated. He said: I said: And what is the necessitated? He said: The mother of the (child’s) raiser, or a hired wet nurse, or a bought servant. Whatever is by the like of that, is established.
